identity.title: ALMA and Herschel observations of the prototype dusty and polluted white dwarf G29-38
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: ALMA Cycle 0 and *Herschel* $^1$ PACS observations are reported for the prototype, nearest, and brightest example of a dusty and polluted white dwarf, G29-38.

evidence.quote: At 13.6 pc, G29-38 is the nearest example of a disk-polluted white dwarf and also the brightest by an order of magnitude

question.value: Is there an outlying, cold parent planetesimal population at 1-100 AU around the dusty, polluted white dwarf G29-38 that can be detected with ALMA and Herschel?

evidence.quote: These long wavelength programs attempted to detect an outlying, parent population of bodies at $1-100$ AU, from which originates the disrupted planetesimal debris

analysis_steps.goal: Reduce Herschel PACS data and measure aperture photometry

method.value: Standard PACS photometer processing in HIPE, photProject maps, high-pass filtering, point-source aperture photometry; upper limit = flux + 3 sigma

evidence.quote: The derived upper limits for G29-38 are the flux measured in the source apertures $+3\sigma$

key_parameters.value: Aperture radii 5" and 8"; filter widths 66" and 102"; aperture corrections 1.94 and 1.90

evidence.quote: aperture corrections applied; 1.94 and 1.90 for the 100 and 160 $\mu$m bands respectively
The source was assumed to be point-like and photometry was performed using apertures.

method.value: Pipeline-processed images; RMS adopted as 1 sigma, 3 sigma upper limits; combined band 6+7 image

evidence.quote: upper limits for unresolved emission from the science target were taken to be $3\sigma$

analysis_steps.goal: Convert limits to fractional dust luminosity vs radius

method.value: f = 3.4e9 F_nu d^2 X_lambda / (r^2 B_nu(lambda,T)); ALMA limits divided by number of beams per ring circumference when resolved

evidence.quote: The plotted ALMA sensitivities were corrected for such resolved cases by assuming a face on disk and dividing by the number of beams per ring circumference.

assumptions.value: Blackbody grains, face-on disk, distance 13.6 pc

evidence.quote: by assuming a face on disk

method.value: m(T)=F_nu d^2/(kappa B_nu(T)) using 870 um limit of 0.17 mJy/beam, ring radii up to 60 AU

the average value of dust opacity is adopted here, $\kappa=1.7$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 870 $\mu$m

assumptions.value: Optically thin, circular face-on thin ring

evidence.quote: the calculations assume a simple, circular, and face-on ring of radial thickness much less than the beam size
Using the Common Astronomy Software Applications package, a band 6 and 7, beam-combined image was created
The PACS data were reduced using the *Herschel* Interactive Processing Environment (HIPE) version 7.0.
No associated emission sources were detected in any of the data down to $L_{\rm IR}/L_*\sim10^{-4}$
generally ruling out cold dust masses greater than $10^{24}-10^{25}$ g

findings_qualitative.value: Several projected A-star debris disks would have been detectable with ALMA but not Herschel or Spitzer, suggesting such disks are depleted by the white dwarf phase.

evidence.quote: several of the brightest A-star debris disk projections were readily detectable in the ALMA (but not *Herschel* or *Spitzer*) observations

claims.hypothesis: Cold outer planetesimal belts around G29-38 are detectable with Herschel/ALMA
claims.experiment: Herschel PACS 100/160 um and ALMA Band 6/7 continuum observations
claims.finding: No bright cold disk; consistent with collisional depletion models

evidence.quote: Overall, these null detections are consistent with models of long-term collisional evolution in planetesimal disks

limitations_admitted.value: Early, shallow ALMA data with limited antennas; projections assume no further collisional evolution

evidence.quote: ALMA in early and relatively shallow observations at 870 and 1305 $\mu$m

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust mass limits depend strongly on assumed opacity and ring geometry

reproducibility.score_reason: Simple non-detection analysis with formulas but sparse processing details.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are upper limits and imaging settings are not stated.
